title: Lightning Is 5 Times Hotter Than the Sun's Surface

scenes.text: A lightning bolt is five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The US National Weather Service puts it at around fifty thousand degrees Fahrenheit.
The Sun's surface sits at roughly ten thousand degrees. So a strip of air above your house briefly beats a star.
The air heats so fast it explodes outward, then snaps back as it cools. That bang is thunder.
It happens because a huge electric current is forced through a channel of air only a few inches wide.
So next time you hear thunder, remember: that's air exploding from the heat of a star.

description:
A lightning bolt is five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The US National Weather Service says lightning heats the air in its path to around 50,000 degrees Fahrenheit, while the Sun's surface is roughly 10,000 degrees.
The air expands so fast it explodes outward, and that bang is thunder.
Have you ever been close enough to feel one?
